issues.spec_citation: CQL Reference v1.5.3 Appendix B, List Operators, Skip: null count returns the entire list; negative count returns an empty list.
issues.evidence: Fresh probe `.temp/qa/cql19_skeptic_probe.py`: `SELECT Skip([1, 3, 5], NULL)` returned SQL NULL on forced Python fallback, native-loaded registration, and no-Python C++; expected `[1, 3, 5]`. `SELECT Skip([1, 3, 5], -1)` also returned SQL NULL on all three surfaces; expected `[]`. Translated CQL `Skip({1, 3, 5}, null)` and `Skip({1, 3, 5}, -1)` had the same failures.
issues.root_cause: The public Skip macro and query-form skip lowering used DuckDB slicing/null comparison semantics that propagated NULL for null and negative counts instead of applying CQL list-operator rules.
issues.resolution: Updated Skip macro semantics and routed query-form skip through Skip instead of LIST_SLICE; added parity coverage for null and negative counts.

issues.spec_citation: CQL Reference v1.5.3 Appendix B, List Operators, Properly Includes / Properly Included In: list inclusion uses equality semantics, with null elements considered equal.
issues.evidence: Fresh probe `.temp/qa/cql19_skeptic_probe.py`: translated `{ 1 'g', 2 'g' } properly includes 1000 'mg'`, `1000 'mg' properly included in { 1 'g', 2 'g' }`, and the list-list variants all returned false on forced Python fallback, native-loaded registration, and no-Python C++; expected true because `1 'g'` equals `1000 'mg'` by Quantity equality.
issues.root_cause: List proper-inclusion translation used DuckDB list_contains/list_has_all semantics, bypassing CQL element equality for Quantity JSON and null list members.
issues.resolution: Routed list proper-inclusion operators through CQLListContainsEq/CQLListHasAllEq, added null-container short-circuits, and hardened helper macro binder behavior for untyped NULL.
issues.verified_in: Architect validation reviewed fresh probe, focused list tests, C++ sqllogictest, WASM/no-Python gate, official CQL list category, full conformance 2822/2822, full pytest 7216 passed / 5 skipped, and diff check.

issues.spec_citation: CQL Reference v1.5.3 Appendix B, List Operators, Union: if either list argument is null, it is considered an empty list.
issues.evidence: Fresh probe `.temp/qa/cql19_skeptic_probe.py`: translated `(null as List<Integer>) union (null as List<Integer>)` lowered to `SELECT NULL` and returned SQL NULL on forced Python fallback, native-loaded registration, and no-Python C++; expected an empty integer list.
issues.root_cause: List union lowering treated both compile-time null list operands as SQL NULL instead of CQL empty-list operands.
issues.resolution: Changed typed null/null list union lowering to produce an empty list and retained CQL distinct-union behavior.
issues.verified_in: Architect validation reviewed fresh probe, focused list tests, C++ sqllogictest, WASM/no-Python gate, official CQL list category, full conformance 2822/2822, full pytest 7216 passed / 5 skipped, and diff check.

issues.spec_citation: CQL Reference v1.5.3 Appendix B, List Operators, Singleton From: a list containing more than one element throws a run-time error.
issues.evidence: Fresh direct parity check: `SELECT SingletonFrom(['a','b'])` raises `InvalidInputException` on the forced Python fallback but returned SQL NULL on native-loaded registration and no-Python C++; expected a runtime error on all public DuckDB surfaces.
issues.root_cause: Native C++ SingletonFrom returned NULL for multi-item lists while Python fallback enforced the CQL runtime-error boundary.
issues.resolution: Changed native C++ SingletonFrom to raise InvalidInputException for multi-item lists and updated sqllogictest/parity tests.
